title: Superactivated carbide-derived carbons with high hydrogenstorage capacity
material_description: Zr-CDC | pristine zirconium carbide-derived carbon, ZrC chlorinated with Cl2 at 800 C for 3 h, not activated
source_location: main.pdf p.3 (journal p.225), Table 1, Zr-CDC row, H2 uptake column (value in parentheses, 1 bar); Fig. 3 (main.pdf p.4) Zr-CDC curve
notes: No separate digitized point: markers of the five curves overlap at 1 bar in Fig. 3 and none could be assigned to this curve. isotherm_id given because the paper presents Table 1 uptake at 20 bar and 1 bar as the capacity of the Fig. 3 isotherms. BET range: P/Po 0.02 to 0.22 (N2 at -196 C). T printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath), 77.15 K. Gravimetric (Hiden IGA, model not named); uptake buoyancy-corrected, assumed carbon density 1.5 g cm-3 (stored in skeletal_density_g_cm3 as the assumed value). Outgassed at 10^-10 bar (1e-5 Pa) and 200 C overnight; duration not numeric. H2 99.9999% purity. Paper does not name excess/absolute/total; basis_inferred excess by instrumental default (gravimetric with buoyancy correction stated). Table 1: total pore volume at P/Po ca. 0.99, micropore surface area and volume by t-plot; NLDFT (N2, slit) pore size maxima 8/13 A not stored as average diameter. Isotherms described as reversible with no hysteresis; branch of individual plotted markers not identified, coded adsorption by rule.
